The '''2021–22 Czech First League''', known as the '''[[Czech First League|Fortuna Liga]]''' is the 29th season of the [[Czech Republic]]'s top-tier [[association football|football]] for professional clubs since its 1993 establishment. [[SK Slavia Prague]] were the reigning champions. The season started on 24 July 2021. The first half of the season had 19 rounds, finishing on 19 December 2021, and the other half commenced on 5 February 2022. The season ended on 14 May 2022 with two extra play-out fixtures on 19 and 22 May 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lfafotbal.cz/clanek/464-aktualni-soutezni-rocnik-skonci-v-lete-2022-o-tyden-drive|title=Aktuální soutěžní ročník skončí v létě 2022 o týden dříve|date=16 November 2021|website=LFA Fotbal|language=cs}}</ref>

The season format was changed back to be played with 16 clubs, each team playing in the league format home and away matches, before the league split into three sections: championship, play-off and relegation groups. The lowest-ranked team was relegated directly to the second league, the two teams positioned 14th and 15th played a play-out with two teams from the second league positioned 2nd and 3rd in a home and away format. This was the fourth season to use [[Video assistant referee|VAR]], featuring it in all matches played. All matches were played on weekdays, with no Friday fixtures expected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2021-22/397929/los-fotbalove-ligy-start-v-cervenci-slavia-ve-zline-derby-v-rijnu.html|title=Los fotbalové ligy: start v červenci, Slavia ve Zlíně. Derby v říjnu|website=[[Blesk]]|publisher=[[Czech News Center]]|date=16 June 2021|language=cs}}</ref>

==Season summary==
This was the fourth season sponsored by the Fortuna betting agency with a contract valid until 2024<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lfafotbal.cz/clanek/207-fortuna-prodlouzila-kontrakt-s-lfa-do-roku-2024|title=Fortuna prodloužila kontrakt s LFA do roku 2024|website=League Football Association|date=12 February 2020|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref> as well as TV broadcasting rights held by O2 TV, which showed all eight matches per week. This was the first season that national broadcaster [[ČT Sport]] did not possess any rights to broadcast any of the fixtures. ''Blesk'' held the rights to the highlights from all matches.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Miloslav|last=Novák|title=Fotbalová liga na placeném kanále, O2 TV získala práva na čtyři roky|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/prvni-liga/fotbalova-liga-o2-tv-fortuna-liga-prenosy.A180618_171315_fotbal_min|newspaper=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|publisher=[[Mafra (company)|Mafra]]|date=18 June 2018|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Fotbalovou ligu opět přinese hlavně O2 TV, část i ČT|url=https://www.mediaguru.cz/clanky/2019/07/fotbalovou-ligu-opet-prinese-hlavne-o2-tv-cast-i-ct/|website=MediaGuru.cz|date=12 July 2019|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref> The 2021–22 season began on 24 July, thirteen days after the [[UEFA Euro 2020]] final. With most of the national team players still released for vacations, [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]], [[AC Sparta Prague|Sparta Prague]] and [[FC Viktoria Plzeň|Plzeň]] started with incomplete first-team squads.

After ten match-weeks the trio recorded one loss each, Viktoria in the 6th round at [[FC Hradec Králové|Hradec Králové]], Sparta in the seventh round in Plzeň and Slavia in round 10 in the Prague Derby at [[Stadion Letná|Letná]] on 3 October 2021. Sparta Prague ended the longest non-winning streak of derby matches after five-and-a-half years at 14 matches. It was also an interruption of Slavia Prague's record unbeaten streak of 54 matches in the first league.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sparta po pěti a půl letech vyhrála derby, Slavia v lize padla po 54 zápasech|url=https://sport.aktualne.cz/fotbal/ceska-liga/300-derby-sparta-slavia/r~94f5ca80247211ec878fac1f6b220ee8/|website=Aktuálně.cz|publisher=[[Economia]]|date=3 October 2021|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref>

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of sixteen teams contest the league, including fifteen sides from the 2020–21 season and the winner of [[2020–21 Czech National Football League|last season's second league]].

;Team promoted to Czech First League

Due to a reduction from 18 to 16 teams, only the winner of the FNL advanced to the first league. On 8 May 2021 [[FC Hradec Králové|Hradec Králové]] defeated [[FK Dukla Prague|Dukla Prague]] 2–1 and secured the promotion with three matches remaining.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-domaci-souteze-druha-liga/395883/hradec-slavi-navrat-do-prvni-ligy-postup-stvrdila-vyhra-s-duklou.html |title=Hradec slaví návrat do první ligy! Postup stvrdila výhra s Duklou|website=Blesk|publisher=Czech News Center|date=8 May 2021|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref> Hradec Králové therefore participated in the top tier after four years of absence.

;Teams relegated from Czech First League

The three lowest positioned teams from the [[2020–21 Czech First League|last season]] were relegated to the Fortuna National League. 

On 8 May 2021, [[SFC Opava|Opava]] became the first team to be relegated to [[Czech National Football League|FNL]] after a 1–1 draw at [[FC Fastav Zlín|Zlín]] with three games remaining, ending their three-year stay in the top flight.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sestřih: Zlín 1–1 Opava {{!}} Slezané jsou prvním sestupujícím do druhé ligy|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/395865/sestrih-zlin-opava-1-1-slezane-jsou-prvnim-sestupujicim-do-druhe-ligy.html|website=Blesk|publisher=Czech News Center|date=8 May 2021|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref>

On 16 May 2021, [[FC Zbrojovka Brno|Zbrojovka]] became the second team to be relegated to [[Czech National Football League|FNL]] after a 1–1 draw at [[FC Slovan Liberec|Slovan Liberec]] with two games remaining, ending their one-year stay in the top flight.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teplice - Č. Budějovice 2:0. Výhra domácích rozhodla o sestupu Brna|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/fotbal-1-liga-rocnik-2020-21/396276/video-teplice-c-budejovice-2-0-vyhra-domacich-rozhodla-o-sestupu-brna.html|website=Blesk|publisher=Czech News Center|date=16 May 2021|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref>

On 23 May 2021, [[1. FK Příbram|Příbram's]] relegation was confirmed following a 0–1 defeat at home against Pardubice with one game remaining, ending their First League tenure after three years.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Antonín|last=Vavrda|title=Rozhodnuto, sestupuje také Starkova Příbram.|url=https://www.lidovky.cz/sport/rozhodnuto-sestupuje-take-starkova-pribram-dekujeme-pardubicim-my-byli-strasni-zlobil-se-kouc-teplic.A210523_192351_ln-sport-fotbal_livs|newspaper=[[Lidové noviny]]|publisher=Mafra|date=23 May 2021|access-date=23 January 2025|language=cs}}</ref>
